title: Barefoot Gen
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In 1945 Hiroshima, six-year-old Gen Nakaoka's family is shunned because his father Daikichi openly opposes the war. The atomic bomb kills much of the family; Gen, his mother and a newborn sister survive and face hunger, radiation sickness and discrimination. Based on author Keiji Nakazawa's own experience, the story follows Gen and fellow orphans into the postwar years.
life_message: Keep living, keep growing like wheat that is trampled, and never forget or excuse those who made war.

content.note: Atomic bombing aftermath with skinless survivors, corpses, maggot-infested burns; frequent beatings (ANN review; AniList Gore, Body Horror; MU Violence).
Family members die trapped in burning house; radiation sickness (ANN review; AniList Tragedy; MU Suffering).
Rape by occupation soldiers referenced (ANN review only, to verify).
Brother volunteers as kamikaze; civilian suicides; grief and loss of family (ANN review; MU Death of Loved One/s).
Teachers beat students, knife threats, crude pranks (ANN review).

dominant: Anti-war humanism; critique of militarism and authority; survival and found family

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Gen answers taunts and bullying with fists (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Father defies wartime rules; authority shown as oppressive (AniList, ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family and found family of orphans carry the story (AniList Found Family).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Humanist anti-war stance; religious figures attacked as corrupt (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Struggle for food and survival dominates (AniList, MU).

folkways.japan: Wartime pressure to conform and revere the emperor is the backdrop; the father's refusal is shown as costly defiance of group harmony.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls it 'a message manga' voicing Nakazawa's strong antiwar beliefs; Gen says the Emperor should apologize.
delivery.note: The anti-war view is stated outright by sympathetic characters; supporters of the war appear mainly as oppressors or profiteers (to verify across volumes).

winners_losers: Survivors and outcasts who keep helping each other get the sympathy; militarists, profiteers and the occupation's indifference are condemned (ANN).
